rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should test a multimodal baseline to assess if combining RNA and image data improves performance. This configuration uses simple encoders (pca_n2000 for RNA, resnet50 for images) with no aggregation or complex fusion, isolating the effect of multimodal integration. It balances exploration by testing the core hypothesis of multimodal benefits without overcomplicating other design choices.

The existing evidence shows that the multimodal config_016 achieved 0.5266 accuracy. Testing config_001 (rna_only with same pca_n2000 encoder) isolates the effect of modality choice, which is critical for determining if multimodal approaches provide value. This comparison directly addresses whether removing image data improves performance, while keeping RNA encoder consistent with the previous experiment.

Existing evidence shows multimodal models (config_016) outperform rna_only (config_001). This experiment tests weighted fusion (vs concat in config_016) to isolate its impact on performance. It builds on the promising multimodal baseline while exploring a key design choice with potential to improve accuracy.

Existing evidence shows multimodal models (config_016: 0.5266 accuracy) outperform RNA-only (config_001: 0.4849). This experiment tests multiprofile (untested in previous multimodal experiments) with avgpool aggregation, which could reveal if profile settings impact performance. It isolates the effect of multiprofile while keeping RNA/image encoders and fusion type consistent, balancing exploration of a key design choice with exploitation of proven components.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings (config_018: 0.6186 accuracy) outperform singleprofile and rna_only baselines. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from concat to weighted in the same high-performing multiprofile setup improves accuracy further. It isolates the effect of fusion strategy while keeping other components (pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool) consistent, allowing us to determine if weighted fusion provides better performance than concatenation in this context.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile settings and weighted fusion yield high accuracy (config_019: 0.6389). This experiment tests replacing the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l while keeping other parameters (pca_n2000, avgpool, weighted fusion) consistent. This isolates the effect of the image encoder's complexity, which could further improve performance. It balances exploitation of proven components with exploration of a more advanced encoder.

The existing evidence shows that config_019 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether switching to transformer aggregation (while keeping RNA encoder, image encoder, profile setting, and fusion method the same) could improve performance. This directly isolates the effect of aggregation method, a key design choice, and balances exploration of promising directions with minimal parameter changes.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_019) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.639). This experiment tests whether switching to transformer aggregation (a more complex method) with the same weighted fusion could further improve performance. It clarifies the impact of aggregation strategy while maintaining the effective fusion approach, balancing exploration of key design choices with exploitation of proven components.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_019) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.639). This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder (pca_n2000 → scvi_n200) while keeping other parameters identical, isolating the impact of the RNA encoder on performance. This is the best use of the final experiment to explore a key design choice with minimal changes, potentially improving accuracy without overcomplicating the model.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, scvi_n200 RNA encoder, and weighted fusion achieve high accuracy (e.g., config_031: 0.6776). This experiment tests replacing the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l in config_031 to determine if a more powerful image encoder improves performance. It isolates the effect of the image encoder while keeping other key components (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted fusion) consistent, maximizing the chance of improving upon the current best.
